q6.answer: The worker selects due schedules with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, so only one worker holds the schedule row. As a backstop, the insert uses UNIQUE (schedule_id, fire_time) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a second insert for the same fire time creates nothing.

q7.answer: It is kept in job_schedules.next_fire_at. It changes when run creation advances it to the first fire time after now(), and when a schedule is disabled (set to NULL) or re-enabled or resumed (recomputed as the first fire time after now()).

q8.answer: The claim query selects one pending or retry_wait run whose next_attempt_at is due, using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, and in the same statement sets it to running with attempt_count+1, claimed_by and heartbeat_at. The row lock means only one worker gets it, and the run is no longer claimable once it is running.

q9.answer: It is kept in job_runs.heartbeat_at, which the running worker refreshes every 30 seconds. The reaper step that every worker runs in its loop notices runs with status running and heartbeat_at older than 2 minutes, using SKIP LOCKED so only one worker handles each.

q10.answer: The wait is recorded on the run itself: status retry_wait and next_attempt_at set to now() plus 1 minute (after attempt 1) or 5 minutes (after attempt 2). The retry starts when the normal claim query finds the run with next_attempt_at <= now(), the same query used for first attempts.

q11.answer: One job_runs row is recorded per fire time of a schedule (unique on schedule_id and fire_time), with its overall status. One job_attempts row is recorded per execution try (unique on run_id and attempt_no), with worker, start and end times, outcome and error.

q12.answer: Its outcome write is conditioned on WHERE id=$run AND status='running' AND attempt_count=$my_attempt (the fencing token). The takeover incremented attempt_count, so the stale write matches 0 rows and the worker discards its result. The attempt row update is also conditioned on outcome='running'.
